classification.difficultyReason: Derive connecting vectors from position vectors and compare their gradients to test collinearity.

children.label: a
children.prompt:
Test whether the points $P$, $Q$ and $R$ are collinear if
$$\overrightarrow{OP}=\begin{pmatrix}-1\\6\end{pmatrix},\quad \overrightarrow{OQ}=\begin{pmatrix}3\\2\end{pmatrix}\quad\text{and}\quad\overrightarrow{OR}=\begin{pmatrix}8\\-3\end{pmatrix}.$$

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\overrightarrow{PQ}&=\overrightarrow{OQ}-\overrightarrow{OP}\\\overrightarrow{PQ}&=\begin{pmatrix}3-(-1)\\2-6\end{pmatrix}\\\overrightarrow{PQ}&=\begin{pmatrix}4\\-4\end{pmatrix}\end{align*}$$
Gradient of $PQ$: $\dfrac{y}{x}=\dfrac{-4}{4}=-1$.
$$\begin{align*}\overrightarrow{QR}&=\overrightarrow{OR}-\overrightarrow{OQ}\\\overrightarrow{QR}&=\begin{pmatrix}8-3\\(-3)-2\end{pmatrix}\\\overrightarrow{QR}&=\begin{pmatrix}5\\-5\end{pmatrix}\end{align*}$$
Gradient of $QR$: $\dfrac{y}{x}=\dfrac{-5}{5}=-1$.
$PQ$ and $QR$ have the same gradient and share $Q$, so $P$, $Q$ and $R$ are collinear.

children.label: b
children.prompt:
Test whether the points $A$, $B$ and $C$ are collinear if
$$\overrightarrow{OA}=3\mathbf{i}+8\mathbf{j},\quad\overrightarrow{OB}=-\mathbf{i}+3\mathbf{j}\quad\text{and}\quad\overrightarrow{OC}=-4\mathbf{i}-\mathbf{j}.$$

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\overrightarrow{AB}&=\overrightarrow{OB}-\overrightarrow{OA}\\\overrightarrow{AB}&=(-\mathbf{i}+3\mathbf{j})-(3\mathbf{i}+8\mathbf{j})\\\overrightarrow{AB}&=-4\mathbf{i}-5\mathbf{j}\end{align*}$$
Gradient of $AB$: $\dfrac{y}{x}=\dfrac{-5}{-4}=\dfrac54$.
$$\begin{align*}\overrightarrow{BC}&=\overrightarrow{OC}-\overrightarrow{OB}\\\overrightarrow{BC}&=(-4\mathbf{i}-\mathbf{j})-(-\mathbf{i}+3\mathbf{j})\\\overrightarrow{BC}&=-3\mathbf{i}-4\mathbf{j}\end{align*}$$
Gradient of $BC$: $\dfrac{y}{x}=\dfrac{-4}{-3}=\dfrac43$.
The gradients differ, so $A$, $B$ and $C$ are not collinear.
